question: An undeformed sedimentary layer is _______ than the layer above and ______ than the layer below.
correct_text: Older—Younger (Law of Superposition: in an undeformed sequence, older strata lie below and younger strata lie above)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 501-505); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 280)

question: Radiometric age is often referred to as ___age.
correct_text: Absolute (Radiometric dating yields numerical/absolute ages in mega-annum Ma or giga-annum Ga)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 282-285); Faure & Mensing (Isotopes: Principles & Applications)

topic: U-Pb Radioactive Decay Series (U-238 to Pb-206)
question: Uranium-238 decays to which of the following daughter isotopes ?
correct_text: Lead-206 (238U decays via alpha and beta cascades to stable 206Pb with t_1/2 = 4.47 Ga)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 284); Dickin (Radiogenic Isotope Geology, Ch. 5)

topic: Relative Dating Principles in Historical Geology
question: Which of the following is used by geologists to determine the relative age in a rock sequence ?
correct_text: All of these (Stratigraphic superposition, fossil succession, and cross-cutting relationships collectively establish relative chronologies)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 281)

topic: Geologic Time Scale: Paleozoic vs Mesozoic Periods
question: Paleozoic does not include :
correct_text: Jurassic (Jurassic belongs to the Mesozoic Era, flanked by Triassic and Cretaceous; Paleozoic spans Cambrian to Permian)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 286-289); Gradstein et al. (GTS 2020)

question: _____ pushed gas and dust particles out of the solar nebula by the light from the sun.
correct_text: Radiation pressure (Solar photon radiation pressure and T-Tauri stellar winds swept volatile gases out of the inner accretionary disk)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Earth Structure, Ch. 1)

topic: Oceanic Crust Accretion at Mid-Oceanic Rifts
question: | The youngest part of the earth crust are :
correct_text: Mid-oceanic rifts (New oceanic lithosphere is continually created at divergent spreading axes, representing zero-age crust)
textbook_ref: Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, 3rd Ed., Ch. 5); Van der Pluijm & Marshak (Ch. 16)

question: The flowpattems found on the surface of Mars suggest that :

options.A: Mars is a water rich planet
options.B: Climate on Mars was different in the past

correct_text: Climate on Mars was different in the past (Valley networks and outflow channels demonstrate an ancient warm, wet Noachian climate)
textbook_ref: Carr (The Surface of Mars, Cambridge Univ. Press); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 12)

question: The crust of Mars is believed to —________ than earths.
correct_text: be much stronger (A thick, cold single-plate lithosphere supports massive volcanic loads like Olympus Mons without subduction)
textbook_ref: Turcotte & Schubert (Geodynamics, 3rd Ed., Ch. 3); Carr (The Surface of Mars)

question: Graded bedding is developed due to:

options.B: Action of waves along the coasts
options.C: Geological action of wind in deserts
options.D: Dumping of debris carried by glaciers

correct_text: Turbidity currents (Decelerating subaqueous density flows deposit classic fining-upward Bouma Ta divisions)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 2, pp. 48-52); K.M. Bangar (p. 142)

question: Foliation in a rock facilitates breaking :

options.C: At right angles to the plane of foliation

correct_text: Along the planes of foliation (Planar alignment of phyllosilicates creates weakness planes with minimal tensile strength)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, 2nd Ed., Ch. 12, pp. 260-272); K.M. Bangar (p. 210)

question: Half life of U-235 is :
correct_text: 0.71 x 10^3 my (The decay half-life of 235U to 207Pb is 704 million years / 0.704 Ga)
textbook_ref: Dickin (Radiogenic Isotope Geology, Ch. 5); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 284)

question: The process involved in the formation of unconformity are :
correct_text: Deposition, upheaval and erosion (Sedimentation is interrupted by tectonic uplift, subaerial denudation/planation, and renewed subsidence)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 220-224); K.M. Bangar (pp. 165-170)

question: Advantage of Remote Sensing data is:
correct_text: Synoptic view (Broad spatial footprint providing regional architectural perspective unavailable from ground surveys)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand & Ralph W. Kiefer (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 1, pp. 1-15)

topic: Magnetic Field Intensity SI & MKS Units
question: Magnetic field strength in MKS units is:
correct_text: Tesla (The SI/MKS unit of magnetic flux density B is the Tesla T = Wb/m^2; CGS unit is Gauss)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, 2nd Ed., Ch. 5, pp. 280-285)

question: Match the List — | with List — II and select the correct answer in the codes given below : List - | List - Il (a) Zaphrentis (i) Brachiopoda (b) Cidaris (ii), Anthozoa (c) Terebratula (iii) Trilobita (d) Olenellus (iv) _Echinoidea (v) Gastropoda
correct_text: (ii), (iv), (i), (iii) [Zaphrentis: Anthozoa; Cidaris: Echinoidea; Terebratula: Brachiopoda; Olenellus: Trilobita]
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 4-8); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 310-345)

question: Which of the following came first ir the stratigraphic record ?
correct_text: Conifers (Gymnosperm conifers arose in the Late Carboniferous ~310 Ma, preceding Dinosaurs ~235 Ma, Birds ~150 Ma, and Angiosperms ~130 Ma)
textbook_ref: Michael J. Benton (Vertebrate Palaeontology, 4th Ed.); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 350-355)

topic: Rheology of Rock Folding & Ductile Deformation
question: Folding occurs when rocks behave asi—__ ==;
correct_text: Ductile solids (Folding represents continuous ductile strain without macroscopic loss of cohesion under high confining pressure)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 10 & 11, pp. 215-245); Ramsay & Huber (Techniques of Modern Structural Geology)

question: The combined effect of water, boron and fluorine is called :
correct_text: Tourmalinization (B-F-H2O rich pneumatolytic fluids metasomatize granitic wall-rocks to schorl/tourmaline rock)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, pp. 430-435); Bangar (p. 115)

topic: Fluvial Levee Breaching & Crevasse Splay Deposition
question: Crevasse splays are associated with : .
correct_text: Natural levees (During overbank flooding, levee breaching channels sediment into adjacent floodbasins as crevasse splay lobes)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 8, pp. 250-254); K.M. Bangar (p. 32)

topic: Penrose Ophiolite Suites as Obducted Oceanic Crust
question: Remnants of oceanic crust is represented by :
correct_text: Ophiolite (On-land pseudostratigraphic fragments of oceanic lithosphere: peridotite, gabbro, sheeted dikes, pillow basalt, and chert)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 13, pp. 260-268); Kearey et al. (Global Tectonics)

question: Which of the following reflects the maximum amount of incoming solar radiations ?
correct_text: Fresh snow (Freshly fallen snow exhibits the highest planetary albedo of 0.80–0.90 / 80–90%)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 1); Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics)

topic: Geochronologic Hierarchy: Eons of Geologic Time
question: The greatest expanses of geologic time are referred toas____.
correct_text: Eons (The largest formal geochronologic geodivisions: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic, and Phanerozoic)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, p. 508); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 286)

question: Acombination of shallow earthquake, volcanism and contact meta- morphism characterizes a :
correct_text: Spreading center (Characterized by shallow seismicity <= 10 km, basaltic fissure eruptions, and steep thermal/contact metamorphic gradients)
textbook_ref: Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, Ch. 5 & 6); Fowler (The Solid Earth)

question: Corals belongs to ____S class.
correct_text: Anthozoa (Corals, sea anemones, and sea pens belong to Class Anthozoa, lacking a medusoid stage)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 5); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 315-320)

question: What is Paleoichnology ?
correct_text: Study of trace fossils (The study of biogenic sedimentary structures including tracks, trails, burrows, and borings)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 4, pp. 102-108); Adolf Seilacher (Trace Fossil Analysis)

topic: Body Wave Kinematics: Primary P-Wave Arrival
question: If an earthquake occurs at a depth of 118 kms. from a recording station which wave will be recorded first ?
correct_text: Primary wave (Compressional P-waves travel fastest through the Earth interior and arrive first at seismographs)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 145-155); K.M. Bangar (pp. 230-234)

question: In our solar system, which planet has a moon with a mass closest to its own ?
correct_text: Earth (The Moon's mass is ~1/81.3 of Earth's mass, creating the largest satellite-to-primary mass ratio of any major planet)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 8)

question: Lysimeter is used to measure :
correct_text: Evapotranspiration (A lysimeter directly measures actual evapotranspiration and percolation loss from an isolated soil column)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 3, p. 55); Todd & Mays (Groundwater Hydrology)

question: Meteorites containing 50% of silicates are :
correct_text: Pallasites (Stony-iron meteorites containing approximately equal proportions of Fe-Ni metal and silicate olivine crystals)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry, Ch. 2); McSween (Meteorites and Their Parent Planets)

question: The dominance of prismatic minerals in a foliated structure is called :
correct_text: Nematoblastic (Parallel alignment of prismatic or acicular minerals such as amphiboles and sillimanite in foliated rocks)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 23, pp. 470-475); Bangar (p. 132)

question: Zoning in metamorphism was proposed by :
correct_text: Grubemann and Becke (Proposed Epizone, Mesozone, and Katazone based on depth, hydrostatic pressure, and temperature)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, p. 422); Bangar (p. 128)

topic: Snow vs Cloud Discrimination via SWIR Band
question: In remote sensing to differentiate snow from clouds —___ band region is used.
correct_text: Middle infrared (Snow absorbs strongly in the 1.55–1.75 µm SWIR region while water clouds remain highly reflective)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 6, pp. 385-390)

question: Gneisses are characterized by :
correct_text: Banded structure (Gneisses exhibit alternating compositional bands of light felsic and dark mafic minerals)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 23, p. 472); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 195); Bangar (p. 135)

question: Fossil content of alimentary canal of animals are known as —_.
correct_text: Coprolites (Fossilized excrement preserving dietary evidence, intestinal morphology, and alimentary contents)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 1); Mahapatra (p. 302)

topic: Equine Evolution: First Appearance of Eohippus
question: Ancestors of horse made their first appearance in:
correct_text: Eocene (The earliest horse ancestor Hyracotherium/Eohippus appeared in the Early Eocene ~55 Ma)
textbook_ref: Michael J. Benton (Vertebrate Palaeontology, Ch. 10); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 358)

question: Gneiss formed from sedimentary rock is called :
correct_text: Para gneiss (A gneiss derived from a sedimentary protolith such as greywacke or shale; orthogneiss is igneous-derived)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, p. 425); Bangar (p. 136)

topic: Plate Tectonic Controls on High-Grade Metamorphism
question: Severe degree of metamorphism in rock is in those :

options.C: Situated at center of the plates
options.D: Irrespective of the place, the degree is same everywhere

correct_text: Situated near plate boundaries (Subduction complexes and collisional orogenic belts focus extreme pressure, temperature, and devolatilization)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 21, pp. 438-445); Kearey et al. (Global Tectonics, Ch. 11)

question: In which metamorphism there is almost no or little new mineral is formed ?
correct_text: Dynamic metamorphism (Mechanical crushing, brecciation, and granulation along fault zones without significant neo-crystallization)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 21, p. 427); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 129)

question: Theterm including both cleavage and schistosity :
correct_text: Foliation (The general term encompassing all penetrative planar fabric elements in deformed rocks including cleavage and schistosity)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, 2nd Ed., Ch. 12, pp. 260-265); Ramsay & Huber

topic: Igneous Grain Size Scales: Medium-Grained Textures
question: Grain size of 5mm to 1 mmis termed as:
correct_text: Medium grained (Grain diameter between 1 mm and 5 mm corresponds to medium-grained phaneritic rocks like microgranite and dolerite)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 2, pp. 25-28); Bangar (p. 95)

question: Porphyritic texture is not influenced by:
correct_text: Difference in molecular construction (Porphyritic texture results from two-stage cooling or contrasting nucleation vs growth rates, not molecular construction differences)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 3, pp. 40-48); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 172)

topic: Igneous Chilled Margins in Hypabyssal Sills
question: The upper and lower margins of sills are relatively :
correct_text: In fine grain size (Rapid conductive heat loss to cool country rock creates a fine-grained or aphanitic chilled margin)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 4, pp. 60-65); K.M. Bangar (p. 88); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 165)

question: What type of lava leads to the formation of laccoliths ?
correct_text: Viscous lava (Viscous silicic to intermediate magmas resist lateral spreading and arch overlying strata into a mushroom dome)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 4, pp. 62-64); K.M. Bangar (p. 89); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 166)

question: The geology of Venus appears to be dominated by :
correct_text: Volcanisms (Magellan radar mapping reveals that >80% of Venus is covered by vast volcanic plains, shield volcanoes, and coronae)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry); Turcotte & Schubert (Geodynamics, Ch. 1)

question: The rock which is well polished by wind abrasion is called :
correct_text: Ventifacts (Pebbles and cobbles shaped, faceted, polished, and fluted by wind-blown sand abrasion in desert environments)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2, pp. 18-20); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 55)

topic: Fold Plunge Measurement: Trend & Plunge Angle
question: The plunge ofa fold is measured by :
correct_text: Both direction and degree (Plunge requires both the vertical inclination angle and the azimuth/trend direction of the hinge line)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 10, pp. 215-220); Bangar (p. 185)

topic: Universal Gravitational Constant (G) in CGS Units
question: The universal gravitational constant (G) in CGS units is :
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, 2nd Ed., Ch. 2, pp. 45-50)

topic: Structural Geology Strike Definition of Planar Features
question: Bearing ofa line of intersection of the fault plane and horizontal is called :
correct_text: Strike (The compass bearing of the horizontal line of intersection between an inclined plane and the horizontal reference plane)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 1, pp. 12-16); K.M. Bangar (p. 172)

topic: Shear Zone Rheology & Ductile Shear Displacement
question: Thenature of placement in the shear zone is :
correct_text: Ductile (Shear zones are tabular zones of localized continuous ductile shear strain without loss of material continuity)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 15, pp. 340-365); Ramsay & Huber

question: Finely pulverized, clay like powdered rock material is :
correct_text: Gouge (Finely pulverized, clay-like non-cohesive fault rock produced by frictional attrition in shallow fault zones)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 8, pp. 170-175); K.M. Bangar (p. 195)

topic: Extensional Tectonics: Horst and Graben Physiography
question: Horst and graben are physiographic features of ___..__ faults.
correct_text: Normal (Horst and graben structures are uplifted blocks and down-dropped valleys bounded by conjugate normal faults)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 17, pp. 390-405); Bangar (p. 198)

question: Open joints are gradually enlarged due to:
correct_text: Weathering (Chemical dissolution by acidic water and physical frost wedging enlarge open rock joints into wide fissures)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 8, pp. 155-160); Mahapatra (p. 215)

question: Gutenberg discontinuity exists at a depth of :
correct_text: 2900 kms (The seismic discontinuity at 2891 km depth separating the silicate lower mantle from the liquid iron outer core)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 165-170); Bangar (p. 235)

topic: Hans Cloos Joint System: Q-Joints (Cross Joints)
question: Joints traversing linear structures at right angles are :
correct_text: Q joints (Querklüfte / cross joints oriented perpendicular to the fold axis or linear flow fabric)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 7, pp. 145-150); K.M. Bangar (p. 205)

question: How and what are the polygonal cracks related to ?
correct_text: Directly related to tensile forces (Volumetric contraction during desiccation or thermal cooling generates isotropic planar tensile stress)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 4, pp. 95-98); Bangar (p. 145)

question: Rhyolitic magma rich in K, Al, Na and SiO₂ typicaly are produced by the meting of ______ and are associated with___________ eruptions.
correct_text: Continental crust, highly explosive (Partial melting of hydrous continental crust generates high-silica, viscous, volatile-rich explosive magmas)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 11, pp. 220-228); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 168)

topic: Caldera Formation: High Viscosity, Gas & Volume
question: Magma viscosity, volatiles and volume are all very high, a common landform that results is
correct_text: A caldera (Emptying of shallow magma chambers during catastrophic paroxysmal pyroclastic eruptions triggers roof collapse)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 4, pp. 68-72); K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, p. 75)

question: A sedimentary that indicates a warm climate is —________..
correct_text: Limestone (Warm, clear, shallow tropical waters promote biological and physicochemical CaCO3 precipitation)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 6, pp. 159-165); Bangar (p. 148)

question: The late Cenozoic ice age began about ___..
correct_text: 3 million years ago (Northern Hemisphere continental ice sheets initiated in the Late Pliocene ~2.7–3.0 Ma)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16); Lowrie (Ch. 5)

topic: Mantle Proportions: Earth Volume & Mass Fractions
question: The earth structure ‘Mantle’ constitutes :
correct_text: 83% by volume and 68.6% by mass (The Earth's mantle comprises ~83-84% of total volume and ~67-68% of total planetary mass)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3); Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry)

question: The initiation of metamorphism is indicated by :
correct_text: Chlorite (The transition from diagenesis into lower greenschist facies metamorphism is marked by chlorite neo-crystallization)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, pp. 428-432); Bangar (p. 130)

topic: Photogrammetry: Principal Point of Aerial Photographs
question: Geometric center of an aerial photograph is called :
correct_text: Principle point (The intersection of fiducial lines defining the geometric center of an aerial photograph)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 3, pp. 140-145)

question: Line joining places having equal degree of cloudiness is known as
correct_text: Isonephs (Lines on a map connecting points of equal average cloud cover or cloudiness)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, Ch. 2); Strahler (Physical Geography)

topic: Earth Core Structure: Solid Fe-Ni Inner Core
question: Which of the following is true about the inner core ?

options.A: It is believed to be semi solid body
options.B: Itis believed to be solid body
options.C: It is believed to be liquid body
options.D: It is believed to be gaseous body

correct_text: It is believed to be solid body (Inge Lehmann in 1936 discovered the solid inner core from P-wave PKIKP reflections)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 3, pp. 165-172); Bangar (p. 236)

topic: Weathering Regime Mismatches: Tropical vs Mechanical
question: Identify the pair mismatched :

options.A: Cold and humid — both mechanical and chemical weathering
options.C: Hot and humid — Mechanical weathering is pre-dominant
options.D: Hot and dry — Mechanical weathering is pre — dominant

correct_text: Hot and humid — Mechanical weathering is pre-dominant (Hot and humid climates are dominated by profound chemical weathering, not mechanical)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 1, pp. 8-12); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 28)

question: Which of the following is not true in case of drag fold ?

options.A: The axes of the drag folds are parallel to those of major folds
options.B: The drag folds plunge in the same manner as the major folds
options.C: The layers on the upper side of the drag fold slides away from synclincal axis
options.D: The axes of the drag folds are not parallel to those of the major folds '

correct_text: The axes of the drag folds are not parallel to those of the major folds (Pumpelly's Rule dictates that minor drag fold axes ARE strictly parallel to major fold axes)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 11, pp. 240-245); Ramsay & Huber

question: Asand ridge connecting an island to the mainland or to another island is a:
correct_text: Tombolo (A wave-refraction deposited spit or sand bar connecting an offshore island to the mainland)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 4, pp. 62-65); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 82)

question: Equatorial radius of planet earth is :
correct_text: 6378 Kms (The WGS-84 semi-major equatorial radius of Earth is a = 6,378.137 km)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 2, pp. 55-60); Bangar (p. 2)

topic: Joint Set Geometry: Cuboidal Block Fragmentation
question: Three sets of Joints are more or less equally spaced results in :
correct_text: Cuboidal block (Three mutually perpendicular, equally spaced joint sets dissect rock masses into orthogonal cuboidal blocks)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 7, pp. 145-148); K.M. Bangar (p. 204)

question: Karst topography is developed due to:
correct_text: Ground water (Percolating carbonic-acid charged groundwater dissolves limestone to form sinkholes, caves, and karst valleys)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 3, pp. 45-52); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 68-75)

question: Block diagram gives :
correct_text: Three dimensional view (Block diagrams display structural geometry, surface topography, and subsurface cutaways in pseudo-3D)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 1); K.M. Bangar (p. 175)

question: Residual masses of weak rock capped by harder rock is a :
correct_text: Pedestal rock (A residual mushroom rock where weak rock at the base is preferentially eroded by saltating sand grains below a resistant cap)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2, p. 20); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 56)

question: Aerial photographs are taker from: nes
correct_text: Aircraft (Standard metric aerial photogrammetric surveys are flown on fixed-wing manned aircraft)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 2 & 3)

question: Within the continental margin, deep, steep sided valleys known as —_—_—. are seen
correct_text: Submarine canyons (Steep-sided V-shaped valleys incised into continental shelves and slopes by turbidity currents and mass wasting)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 10, pp. 310-315); Bangar (p. 68)

question: Which of the following is not true of deep ocean trenches ?

options.A: They are long and narrow depressions
options.B: They are sites where plates plunge back into the mantle
options.D: They may act as sediment traps

correct_text: They are geologically very stable (Trenches are the most tectonically active zones on Earth, host to megathrust earthquakes and volcanism)
textbook_ref: Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, Ch. 7, pp. 160-175); Lowrie (Ch. 1)

topic: Coastal Denudation: Sea Stacks & Wave Erosion
question: An isolated rock left behind as an island as a coast erodes :
correct_text: Stack (An isolated vertical pillar of rock left standing offshore after collapse of a coastal sea arch)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 4, p. 64); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 80)

question: Deltas where deposition and wave action are roughly equal :

options.A: Build long peninsulas into the sea

correct_text: Have smoothly curving fronts (Equal fluvial deposition and marine wave rework creates smooth, cuspate, wave-dominated arcuate deltas)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 9, pp. 275-285); Bangar (p. 35)

topic: Satellite Attitude Variations: Roll, Pitch, and Yaw
question: Roll, pitch and yaw are __ errors.
correct_text: Geometric (Angular rotational oscillations around sensor XYZ axes distort ground coordinates into geometric image errors)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 7, pp. 480-485)

question: Albite developing in a rock at the cost of a pre existing mineral is :
correct_text: Metasomatism (Sodium-rich hydrothermal fluid exchange replacing calcic plagioclase or K-feldspar with secondary albite)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, pp. 430-435); Bangar (p. 116)

question: Migmatites commonly show : .
correct_text: Ptygmatic fold (Tortuous, meandrine, disharmonic folding of competence-contrasted granitic leucosome veins in ductile migmatitic gneisses)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 23, p. 480); Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, p. 250); Bangar (p. 138)

topic: Geological Rates of Landform Construction: Cinder Cones
question: Which of the following can form ina shortest interval of time ?
correct_text: Volcanic cone (Monogenetic cinder/scoria cones can form in days to months, e.g. Parícutin 1943, unlike soil or river valleys)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 5, pp. 72-76); Mahapatra (p. 140)

topic: GIS Data Structures: Attribute vs Spatial Data
question: Attribute data is also known as :
correct_text: Information (Attribute data represents non-spatial descriptive tabular properties linked to spatial vector geometries)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, 4th Ed., Ch. 3)

topic: Standard False Color Composite (FCC): Urban Signatures
question: In a FCC data, the urban area can be identified by __--_-_ colour.
correct_text: Cyan (In standard NIR-Red-Green FCC, built-up urban concrete and asphalt reflect in blue-green bands, rendering cyan to bluish-gray)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 4, pp. 220-225)

question: Scintillation counter is used for :
correct_text: Redioactive survey (Measures gamma radiation emitted by radioisotopes 40K, 238U, and 232Th via thallium-doped NaI crystals)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 4); Kearey et al. (Exploration Geophysics)

question: Palynology mainly deals with :
correct_text: Spores and pollens (Palynology is the organic-walled microfossil discipline focusing on acid-resistant plant spores, pollens, and dinoflagellates)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 12); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 520)

question: Glossopteris occurs during:
correct_text: Permian — Triassic period (The tongue-shaped seed fern Glossopteris flourished across southern Gondwana during Permian and early Triassic times)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 355-358); Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma)

question: Planktons are those forms which are :
correct_text: Floating near surface (Plankton are passively floating or weakly swimming organisms dwelling in the pelagic sunlit photic zone)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 2); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 100)

topic: Chronostratigraphy Hierarchy: Series between Stage & System
question: Chronostratigraphic unit ranking above stage and below system is :
correct_text: Series (In chronostratigraphic hierarchy: Eonothem > Erathem > System > Series > Stage)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 505-510); Mahapatra (p. 287)

topic: Paleobotanical Chronological Evolution of Plant Genera
question: Consider the following and give correct chronological sequence : () — Lepidodendron - QW) Pfilophyitum (li) ~Palmoxyion (IV) Glossopteris
correct_text: (I), (IV), (II), (III) [Lepidodendron (Carboniferous) -> Glossopteris (Permian) -> Ptilophyllum (Jurassic) -> Palmoxylon (Tertiary)]
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 11 & 12); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 350-360)

question: Earth magnetic field has reversed itself___..__ times.
correct_text: 3-6 times (During the late Cenozoic, geomagnetic polarity reversals occur at an average frequency of 4-5 reversals per million years)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 5, pp. 300-310); Kearey et al. (Global Tectonics)

question: Ejecta from a volcano are collectively known as _____.
correct_text: Tephra (The collective term for all airborne fragmental volcanic ejecta regardless of clast size or composition)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 2, pp. 30-35); Bangar (p. 78)

topic: Lindgren's Law of Constant Volume in Metasomatism
question: The total volume of the rock is changed after metasomatism :
correct_text: Remains same (Waldemar Lindgren's volume law dictates that equal-volume metasomatic replacement occurs without bulk expansion/shrinkage)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 21, p. 433); Guilbert & Park (The Geology of Ore Deposits); Bangar (p. 116)

topic: Wentworth Grain Size Scale: Granule Gravel
question: The particle size of a gravel is :
correct_text: 2—4mm (On the Wentworth clastic particle scale, granule gravel spans 2 mm to 4 mm / -1 to -2 phi)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 3, pp. 60-65); Bangar (p. 140)

question: High temperature metamorphic mineral assemblage is converted into an assemblage stable at low ‘temperature is :
correct_text: Retrogressive Metamorphism (Diaphthoresis: conversion of high-temperature mineral assemblages to lower-grade hydrous phases during cooling)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21, p. 435); Bangar (p. 131)

question: Buchites occurring as xenoliths in basalts or diabase are the product of: .
correct_text: Pyro Metamorphism (Pyrometamorphism produces buchite: vitrified, partially melted xenolithic shale/sandstone in sanidinite facies)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 21, p. 427); Turner & Verhoogen (Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology)

topic: Orbital Mechanics in Remote Sensing Platforms
question: The path followed by a satellite is referred to as its :
correct_text: Orbit (The mathematical geometric path described by a satellite revolving around Earth under gravitational Keplerian laws)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 6, pp. 360-365)

question: LANDSAT has a swath width of —___. Kms.
correct_text: 185 (Landsat 1 through 9 missions feature a constant nominal cross-track swath width of 185 kilometers / 115 miles)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 6, p. 370)

topic: Planck's Law & Absolute Zero Thermal Radiation
question: All matters at temperature above —_________ °C continuously emits electromagnetic rediation.
correct_text: - 273°C (All matter at thermodynamic temperatures above absolute zero 0 K / -273.15 °C continuously radiates electromagnetic energy)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 1, pp. 5-10); Lowrie (Ch. 4)

topic: History of Aerial Photography: First Aircraft Flight
question: The first aerial photograph taken from an aircraft was in:
correct_text: 1909 (Wilbur Wright piloted an airplane in Centocelle, Italy, filming and photographing the ground in 1908-1909)
textbook_ref: Thomas M. Lillesand (Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation, Ch. 2, p. 45)

question: Intertrappean beds are. of —_______ origin. .
correct_text: Continental (Fluvio-lacustrine sedimentary beds deposited in freshwater lakes and rivers during volcanic quiescence intervals)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 270-275); Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma)

question: Which typical mineral marks the Deccan Volcanism ?
correct_text: Pyroxene (Deccan tholeiitic basalts are dominated by augite/clinopyroxene and calcic plagioclase labradorite)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Ch. 8, pp. 160-165); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 272); Bangar (p. 105)

topic: Dharwar Craton Structural Grain: Dharwarian Trend
question: The characteristic regional strike direction of Dharwars is :
correct_text: NNW-SSE (The dominant regional strike and fold trend of the Archean Dharwar Supergroup in Karnataka is NNW-SSE)
textbook_ref: Ramakrishnan & Vaidyanadhan (Geology of India, Vol. 1, Ch. 3, pp. 65-80); Mahapatra (p. 260)

question: Which forms have smaller Proloculus.
correct_text: Microspheric (The sexually produced microspheric generation has a tiny proloculus with a large adult multi-chambered test)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 3, pp. 25-30); Mahapatra (p. 312)

topic: Mesozoic Stratigraphy: Marine Jurassic of Kutch
question: The age of Rana of Kutch sediments is:
correct_text: Jurassic (The classic Patcham, Chari, Katrol, and Umia formations record magnificent marine Jurassic ammonite zones)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 265-268); Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma)

topic: Purana Proterozoic Sedimentary Basins of India
question: How many Proterozoic basins are located in India ?
correct_text: 14 (India hosts 14 major Purana Proterozoic sedimentary basins including Cuddapah, Vindhyan, Chattisgarh, and Kaladgi)
textbook_ref: Ramakrishnan & Vaidyanadhan (Geology of India, Vol. 1, Ch. 6, pp. 195-210); Kale & Phansalkar (1991)

topic: Cyclic Marine Transgressions: Jurassic of Kutch
question: Which is the type area of cyclic transgression and regression in India ?
correct_text: Jurassic of Kutch (Repeated eustatic transgressive-regressive cycles deposited rhythmically alternating bioclastic and siliciclastic strata)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 266); Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma)

question: How many sets of thrusts are found in Himalayas ?
correct_text: 4 (The four foundational south-vergent fault systems are: MFT, MBT, MCT, and the extensional STDS/ITSZ)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 18, pp. 415-420); Valdiya (Aspects of Tectonics)

topic: Deccan Large Igneous Province Volcanic Stratigraphy
question: Deccan Volcanism has —_____ cycles of emissions.
correct_text: 15 (The Western Ghats Deccan basalt stratigraphy is divided into 3 subgroups and ~12-15 distinct basaltic formations)
textbook_ref: Subbarao & Hooper (Deccan Volcanics, Geol. Soc. India Mem. 10); Ramakrishnan & Vaidyanadhan

question: The supercontinent that fragmented during 2.2Gais___.
correct_text: Columbia (The Paleoproterozoic supercontinent Columbia/Nuna amalgamated between 2.1-1.8 Ga and fragmented around 1.6-1.4 Ga)
textbook_ref: Kearey, Klepeis & Vine (Global Tectonics, Ch. 12, pp. 310-315); Rogers & Santosh (2002)

question: Which of the following Stratigraphic boundaries is not defined as paleontological criterion ?
correct_text: Pleistocene — Holocene boundary (Formally defined by abrupt post-glacial climatic warming in Greenland NGRIP ice core at 11,700 yr b2k, not fossil extinction)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 512-515); Walker et al. (2009)

question: Which of the following represents the longest time period ?
correct_text: Precambrian (Spans 4.567 Ga to 0.539 Ga, comprising ~88% of Earth's total geological history)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 286-290); Sam Boggs Jr. (Ch. 16)

question: Which of the following fossil groups form the basis for sub-division of Mesozoic ?
correct_text: Ammonites (Rapid evolutionary suture radiation and nektonic dispersal make Ammonoidea the supreme index fossils of the Mesozoic)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 8); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 330-335)

topic: Permian Marine Transgressions: Umaria Marine Bed
question: Which one of the following strati- graphic unit is marine in origin ?
correct_text: Umaria beds (The Umaria Marine Bed in Madhya Pradesh contains marine Productus brachiopods within peninsular Lower Gondwana)
textbook_ref: G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 264); Krishnan (Geology of India and Burma)

question: What is the most commonly agreed age of the Archean — Proterozoic boundary ?
correct_text: 2500ma (The formal IUGS chronometric boundary separating the Archean and Proterozoic Eons is set at 2500 Ma / 2.5 Ga)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, p. 508); Gradstein (GTS 2020)

question: The algal structure which is reported from the Vindhyan rocks are:
correct_text: Stromatolites (Cyanobacterial organosedimentary structures such as Collenia and Conophyton proliferate in Vindhyan carbonates)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 1); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 262)

question: Foraminifera are good index fossils for
correct_text: Cenozoic (Benthic larger foraminifera like Nummulites and planktic forams provide high-resolution Cenozoic biozones)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 3, pp. 30-35); Mahapatra (p. 314)

question: Which are the microfossils that are prominently found in Red sand- stones ?
correct_text: Ostracods (Bivalved calcified micro-crustaceans thrive in continental lacustrine, fluvial, and brackish red sandstones)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology: Invertebrate, Ch. 9); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 525)

question: In the following formations Conodonts can be traced only from —______ environment.
correct_text: Mesozoic marine (Conodonts are strictly marine phosphatic tooth-like micro-chordates restricted to Paleozoic and Triassic marine facies)
textbook_ref: P.C. Jain & M.S. Anantharaman (Palaeontology, Ch. 10); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 524)

question: Uranium mineralisation is mainly associated with :
correct_text: Acid igneous rocks (Uranium is an incompatible, large-ion lithophile element strongly concentrated in late-stage granites and pegmatites)
textbook_ref: Brian Mason (Principles of Geochemistry); Guilbert & Park (The Geology of Ore Deposits); Bangar (p. 118)

question: Precambrian terrains have a geothermal gradient of :
correct_text: 10°C/Kms (Thick, cold, depleted cratonic lithospheric roots maintain very low conductive geothermal gradients of 8–12 °C/km)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 4, pp. 220-225); Turcotte & Schubert (Ch. 4)

question: Coral reef thrive at a temperature of :
correct_text: 22 to 27°C (Reef-building hermatypic scleractinian corals require optimal sea-surface temperatures between 22 °C and 27 °C)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 4, pp. 65-68); Sam Boggs Jr. (p. 165)

question: Residual masses of weak rock capped by harder rock is a:
correct_text: Pedestal rock (Mushroom-shaped landforms developed when harder caprock protects underlying softer strata from complete denudation)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2, p. 20); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 56)

topic: Fluvial Capture & Stream Piracy: Beheaded Streams
question: The stream which has lost parts of © its drainage is called :
correct_text: Beheaded (River capture occurs when an aggressive pirate stream breaches a divide and diverts headwaters, leaving the downstream channel beheaded)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2, pp. 30-33); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 45)

topic: Karst Weathering Residues: Terra Rossa Formation
question: Terra rossa is a characteristic feature of:
correct_text: Karst region (Red insoluble clayey residual soil enriched in Fe-oxides left behind upon dissolution of impure limestone in Mediterranean karst)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 3, p. 50); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 72)

question: The removal of bedrock particles at the tooling action of transported material is known as : z
correct_text: Abrasion (Corrasion: mechanical wearing, scratching, and gouging of bedrock surfaces by tools transported within the moving medium)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2 & 4); G.B. Mahapatra (pp. 35-40)

topic: Structural Drainage Control: Annular Drainage on Domes
question: On an eroded sedimentary dome, the drainage pattern is usually :
correct_text: Annular (Concentric ring-like stream networks developed on eroded breached structural domes and ring complexes along alternating weak rock belts)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 2, p. 28); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 42)

question: Lahar is a type of ___.
correct_text: Debris flow (Lahar is a rapidly moving volcanic mudflow or debris flow of pyroclasts, mud, and water descending a volcanic edifice)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 5, p. 77); G.B. Mahapatra (p. 142)

question: Greenschist facies rocks mainly contain :
correct_text: Chlorite (The diagnostic low-grade metamorphic mineral assemblage of greenschist facies is chlorite + albite + epidote + actinolite)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 25, pp. 520-525); Bangar (p. 130)

question: Wind borne sediment is called
correct_text: Anemoclasts (A.W. Grabau's clastic classification for sediment grains transported and deposited by wind action; hydroclasts by water)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 3); A.W. Grabau (Principles of Stratigraphy)

topic: Rock Mass Engineering Classification: Barton's Q-System
question: Q system of rock classification was developed by :
correct_text: Barton (Developed by Nick Barton, Lien, and Lunde in 1974 at NGI based on RQD, joint sets, roughness, alteration, water, and stress)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 11, pp. 240-245); Bieniawski (Rock Mechanics Design)

topic: Fault Mechanics: Shear Displacements along Fractures
question: Fractures on which identifiable shear displacements are seen are called as:
correct_text: Faults (Fractures across which measurable, identifiable shear displacement or slip has occurred parallel to the surface)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, 2nd Ed., Ch. 8, pp. 165-172); Bangar (p. 190)

topic: Mining Engineering: Rock Blasting Operation Sequence
question: The sequence of rock blasting are :
correct_text: Boring, charging, tamping and firing (Drill blastholes, insert explosive charge, tamp with inert stemming material, and initiate firing)
textbook_ref: S.K. Garg (Mining and Geological Engineering); K.M. Bangar (Ch. 12, pp. 250-255)

topic: Rock Failure Modes: Brittle and Ductile Regimes
question: Rock failure is general of :
correct_text: Both (Rocks exhibit brittle shear/tensile rupture at shallow crustal depths and transition to continuous ductile flow at higher T-P)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 6, pp. 115-125); Jaeger, Cook & Zimmerman

question: Deformation of excavated rock over a long period is called as :
correct_text: Creep behaviour (Continuous, time-dependent strain and deformation under constant sustained deviatoric stress over extended periods)
textbook_ref: Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 6, pp. 128-132); Jaeger et al. (Fundamentals of Rock Mechanics)

topic: Astronomical Coordinates: Hour Angle of Celestial Bodies
question: The angle between the observer's meridian and declination circle of the heavenly body is referred to as :
correct_text: Hour angle (The angular distance measured westward along the celestial equator from the observer's meridian to the declination circle)
textbook_ref: William Lowrie (Fundamentals of Geophysics, Ch. 1); Smart (Textbook on Spherical Astronomy)

question: GIS represents Z-co-co-ordinates in —_______ direction.
correct_text: Vertical (In 3D spatial coordinate systems, X and Y represent horizontal plane coordinates, and Z represents vertical elevation/depth)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, Ch. 3 & 4)

topic: GIS Spatial Analysis: Boolean Logic in Vector Overlays
question: Overlay analysis is based on:
correct_text: Boolean logic (Vector overlay operations execute set-theory Boolean intersection AND, union OR, and difference NOT operations)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, Ch. 14, pp. 310-318)

question: Which of the following is used to build new features by splitting overlapping features and combining attributes where the features overlap ?
correct_text: Union (A topological overlay tool that splits overlapping vector polygons and combines attributes of all inputs into a geometric union)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, Ch. 14, pp. 315-320)

topic: Spatial Data Quality: Valid Features vs Topology Errors
question: Which of the following doesn’t indicate a topology error ?
correct_text: Polygonal features (Polygonal features are valid primitive geometries; gaps, sliver polygons, and unclosed dangles are topological errors)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, Ch. 9, pp. 195-205)

question: A vector data model uses which of the following co-ordinate pair types to build curvature within a line ?
correct_text: Vertices (Points defining line endpoints are nodes; coordinate pairs defining the intermediate shape and curvature are vertices)
textbook_ref: Paul A. Longley et al. (Geographic Information Science and Systems, Ch. 3, pp. 65-70)

question: Detrital rock containing fragments of * only one type of material is :
correct_text: Oligomictic (Detrital rudaceous rocks where clasts are composed of a single stable rock/mineral type, typically vein quartz or chert)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 5, pp. 130-135); Bangar (p. 144)

question: A rock fragment with a diameter between 64 mm to 256 mm, is :
correct_text: A Cobble (On the Wentworth grain size scale, cobbles span 64 mm to 256 mm; pebbles are 4–64 mm, boulders >256 mm)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 3, p. 62); Bangar (p. 140)

question: The complex process of converting newly deposited sediments into an indurated rock is :
correct_text: Lithification (The comprehensive physical and chemical transformation of soft unconsolidated sediment into solid indurated rock)
textbook_ref: Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 5, pp. 138-142); Mahapatra (p. 180)

question: Dolerite is a _________ rock.
correct_text: Hypabyssal basic (A medium-grained subvolcanic basic intrusive rock occurring in dikes and sills with characteristic ophitic texture)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 2, pp. 28-32); Bangar (p. 102)

question: Kaolinisation is chiefly due to ‘superheated steam, aided little by :
correct_text: Fluorine and Boron (Acidic hydrothermal alteration of aluminosilicate feldspars aided by superheated steam and volatile F and B complexes)
textbook_ref: Guilbert & Park (The Geology of Ore Deposits, Ch. 6, pp. 175-185); Bangar (p. 115)

question: Myrmekitic texture is an inter growth between :
correct_text: Plagioclase and quartz (A vermicular or worm-like intergrowth of quartz rods inside sodic plagioclase invading K-feldspar)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 3, pp. 48-52); Bangar (p. 98)

topic: Volcanic Vesicularity: Mafic Scoria vs Pumice
question: Gas cavities in lava which are irregular in shape and numerous is called as :
correct_text: Scoria (Dark, heavy, highly vesicular basaltic or andesitic pyroclasts with irregular, jagged, non-spherical gas cavities)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 2, p. 32); Bangar (p. 104)

question: Which one is a non plastic clay ?
correct_text: China clay (Kaolinite has a rigid 1:1 hydrogen-bonded sheet structure with minimal water absorption, giving low plasticity compared to bentonite/ball clay)
textbook_ref: K.M. Bangar (Principles of Engineering Geology, Ch. 10, pp. 225-228); Mahapatra (p. 240)

question: Garnet variety commonly found in gneisses and schists is :
correct_text: Almandine (Fe3Al2Si3O12 is the classic iron-aluminum garnet diagnostic of medium-to-high grade Barrovian pelitic schists and gneisses)
textbook_ref: John D. Winter (Principles of Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology, Ch. 21 & 28, pp. 580-588); Bangar (p. 135)
